benchmarkQuestion: On source-disjoint Markdown documents from already-exposed project families, how often does Spanish-versus-explicit-English retrieval return a span sufficient for the frozen question, and when Jev receives those exact candidates, does it select sufficient positive evidence or abstain on explicit no-answer questions?
hypotheses: An explicit English query will improve retrieval over the Spanish query for English source documents.
When at least one candidate is returned, Jev will select sufficient evidence on positive questions and abstain on explicit no-answer questions.
Exact fetch and evidence-pack integrity will hold for every valid selected handle.

limits.familyExposure: All three families were previously exposed; these exact sourceRefs and hashes were absent from the local run ledger. The cohort is source-disjoint within known families, not family-independent.

searchProtocol.candidatePolicy: Run Jev separately per non-empty arm using exactly the search-returned handles, with selectionMode=search-results. If an arm returns no candidates, record not-run; do not turn an empty pool into a semantic abstention result.

metrics.reporting: Report Spanish and English arms paired by question. Do not treat paired arms or repeated calls as independent questions. Do not call raw Choice/Noul calibrated confidence.

preflightExcluded.result: First request rejected before provider because maxSnippetChars=500 exceeded the runtime maximum 240. A corrected search smoke succeeded before this plan was frozen.
preflightExcluded.reasonExcluded: The first candidate result was observed before the plan/checksum was frozen; exclude both preflight searches from primary metrics. No Jev call occurred.

reviewMethod.curation: Luna agent curated source-derived questions/labels after checking source hashes and Git state.
